'''John Pagus'''<ref>John Le Page, Johannes Pagus, Jean Le Page, Jean Lepage.</ref> ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|p|eɪ|g|ə|s}}; fl. first half of the 13th century) was a [[scholastic philosopher]] at the [[University of Paris]], generally considered the first [[logician]] writing at the Arts faculty at Paris.<ref>Bertil Malmberg, ''Histoire de la Linguistique'', Paris: Presses universitaires de France, 1991, p. 127.</ref>

==Life==
He is thought to have been a [[Master of Arts]] in the 1220s and to have taught [[Peter of Spain (author)|Peter of Spain]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hansen |first=Heine |title=John Pagus on Aristotle's Categories : a study and edition of the Rationes super Praedicamenta Aristotelis |date=2012 |publisher=Leuven University Press |isbn=978-90-5867-913-0 |location=Leuven |page=83 |oclc=827884193}}</ref> At that time he was writing on [[syncategorematic term]]s.<ref>Sten Ebbesen, Russell L. Friedman (editors), ''Medieval Analyses in Language and Cognition'' (1999), p. 36.</ref><ref>Parts published in [[Henk Braakhuis|H. A. G. Braakhuis]], ''De 13de Eeuwse Tractaten over Syncategorematische Termen''. Vol. I, Ph. Diss., Leiden University, 1979.</ref>

==Works==
*''Appellationes''
*Commentary on the ''[[Sentences]]''
*''Rationes super Predicamenta Aristotelis''
*''Syncategoremata''
